neighbours.label: the restrictive focus 'only' introducing what is claimed instead ('not only is…', '…, only that X'): fires on the word right after 'only'
fire: The audit does not show fraud, only that the books were messy.
His silence proves nothing, only that he was tired.
Not only is the bridge old, it is also unsafe.
The letter does not say she left, only that she was unhappy.
The scan does not mean cancer, only that more tests are needed.
Not only is the food cheap, it tastes wonderful.
The rule does not ban phones, only that they stay silent in class.
We were told nothing, only that the train was delayed.
quiet: The audit took only two days and found the books in order.
His silence lasted only a minute before he spoke again.
The bridge is old and it is also unsafe for trucks.
The letter was only one page long and unsigned.
The scan took only ten minutes at the clinic.
The food is cheap and it tastes wonderful too.
The rule applies only to phones brought into class.
We had only one ticket for the delayed train.

notes: Probe: 'only that' 0.2-0.9, 'not only is/are' ~0.15-0.3, 'the only thing' and 'only then' ~0. Negative pole is concessive 'even'. Near misses keep 'only' as a plain quantity word or drop it.
